stories.headline: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
stories.quickScoop: Widgets, your way. | Photo: Allison Johnson / The Verge Aside from dealing with my calendar, there's one thing I want AI to do: tell me if I'm about to miss the bus.
summary: What I need is a widget.
It needs to tell me real-time arrivals for the bus stop near my house.
Tapping around on my phone screen to open the right app and select my stop will…
I need glanceable information, and I hoped that Android's vibe-coded widget feature could help me out…
It hasn't, to my disappointment, but I still had a good time cooking up other widgets.
stories.whyItMatters: Tools like this change what ordinary people and workers can do day to day, no technical skill required.

dailyChallenge.question: Which of these is the best definition of "AI Hallucination"?
choices: When an AI system confidently states information that is false, made up, or not actually supported by its sources.
An AI technique that determines whether a piece of text expresses a positive, negative, or neutral feeling.
The internal numerical settings a neural network adjusts during training; roughly, the "knowledge dials" that get tuned as the model learns.
Technology that lets computers do things that normally need human thinking, like understanding language, recognizing images, or making decisions.
dailyChallenge.explanation: When an AI system confidently states information that is false, made up, or not actually supported by its sources. Hallucinations are a key reason experts recommend double-checking important facts an AI gives you.

dailyActivity.title: Plan a study schedule that actually fits your week
dailyActivity.learningObjective: How to turn a vague study goal into a concrete plan.
dailyActivity.tryThis: I have [exam/topic] in [X days] and about [Y hours] a week free. Break this into a day-by-day study plan with specific tasks.
dailyActivity.whyItWorks: AI is good at breaking a big, fuzzy goal into small, scheduled steps once you give it real constraints.
